questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the key difference between a demo and a feature tour?
options: A demo is shorter than a feature tour
A feature tour requires more code than a demo
There is no real difference; the terms are interchangeable
A demo follows one realistic scenario end to end, showing why features matter together, rather than showing ten disconnected proofs
questions.explain: A feature tour shows that things exist in isolation; a demo follows a realistic scenario that shows the pieces working together the way they would on a real day.

questions.q: In the six-step demo scenario, what happens immediately after a Service Agent creates a Case linked to an Asset?
options: Renata reviews the Executive Dashboard
The Case to Installation Job Flow runs automatically, creating an Installation_Job__c assigned to a technician
The manufacturer's API is called directly from the Case
A Warranty_Claim__c is created immediately with no technician involvement
questions.explain: Step 2 of the scenario is the record-triggered Flow from Lesson 6 firing automatically to check contract coverage and create the Installation Job.

questions.q: What does a "narration-first, clicks-second" demo script provide that a rigid list of clicks doesn't?
options: A recovery path -- narration that stays true and useful even if a live click fails, letting the story continue
Faster demo execution time
Automatic error handling in the scratch org
A guarantee that no live demo will ever fail
questions.explain: Writing narration that remains accurate even if the live action fails means a frozen screen or failed click doesn't stall the whole demo -- you can keep narrating and show a recent result instead.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when should the technical debt named in Lesson 22's retrospective come up during the demo?
options: At the very start, as a disclaimer before anything is shown
It should never be mentioned under any circumstances, even if asked
As a direct, honest answer if specifically asked, not volunteered unprompted during the walkthrough
Only at the very end, read aloud as a full list
questions.explain: The lesson says technical debt should be answered honestly and specifically if asked, but volunteering it unprompted during a demo undermines confidence in the parts that work well.

questions.q: How many of the capstone's major built pieces does the six-step demo scenario touch, per this lesson?
options: Only the Apex trigger, nothing else
Every major piece of the capstone, each appearing exactly once in the order it would actually fire
Only the reports and dashboards
None -- the demo is purely a slide presentation with no live org
questions.explain: The lesson states the six steps touch nearly every major piece built across the capstone, each appearing once in the order it would naturally occur in a real event.
